items.title: Partial count leaves Netanyahu and Eisenkot short of a majority
items.desc: Projections with half the votes counted put Netanyahu’s bloc on 55 seats and the opposition on 49, with Palestinian parties potentially holding the key to coalition talks.

items.title: Tourists urged to avoid high Himalayas as bad weather looms
items.desc: Heavy rain, snowfall and possible avalanches are forecast from October 28 to November 1, prompting officials to warn trekkers and mountaineers.

items.title: Flavio Bolsonaro and family to receive US visas after leaving Brazil, State Department says
items.desc: His departure came after he missed a court deadline to surrender his passports in a money-laundering probe, threatening to further strain ties between Washington and Brasília.

items.title: Pokhara Avengers sign Sri Lankan wicketkeeper-batter Sadeera Samarawickrama
items.desc: The 31-year-old joins the franchise ahead of Wednesday’s NPL opener against Sudurpaschim Royals, becoming its sixth overseas signing.

items.title: A 228-metre leap above Nepal’s Kaligandaki gorge
items.desc: The suspension bridge linking Kushma and Balewa has become a popular destination for adventure seekers, drawing hundreds of visitors a day to try bungee jumping or watch others take the plunge.

items.title: Could Rahul Yadav be Nepali cricket’s next big thing?
items.desc: A wicket with his first NPL delivery and a miserly four-over spell have put the 17-year-old in the spotlight.

items.title: Users turn to Nepal Telecom as private ISPs raise internet prices
items.desc: The state-owned provider’s discounted annual 30 Mbps fibre package has drawn a surge of interest, but customers have raised concerns about delays, service quality and outdated routers.

items.title: Pokhara Avengers seek first win over Sudurpaschim Royals
items.desc: Pokhara have lost to the Royals in both previous NPL editions, while the two-time finalists are looking to bounce back from an opening-match defeat.

items.title: Israeli exit polls show deadlock, point to setback for Netanyahu
items.desc: Exit polls put Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition neck and neck, with neither securing a parliamentary majority, setting the stage for protracted coalition talks after Israel’s first election since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack.

items.title: Cyclone Arnab begins making landfall in India’s Andhra Pradesh state
items.desc: Thousands were evacuated and transport services disrupted ahead of the cyclone, which was forecast to bring winds of up to 150 kph and a storm surge of up to 2.5 metres.

items.title: Why Nepali film sequels are struggling at the box office
items.desc: From 12 Gaun to Jaari, recent follow-ups have failed to repeat their originals’ commercial success, with critics pointing to recycled plots and an overreliance on popular names.

items.title: Fresh signings deliver immediate results for NPL franchises amid late arrival and PCB-related chaos
items.desc: From Hussain Talat’s match-winning bowling spell for Karnali to Chitwan’s airport-to-ground reinforcements, teams adapt swiftly to sudden changes.

items.title: Two-day weekend boosts tourism across hill stations
items.desc: Introduced as an emergency measure to curb fuel consumption following the US-Israeli war on Iran, the new weekend policy has changed Nepalis’ travel habits and revitalised the country's hospitality sector.

items.title: Malaysia halts recruitment of Nepali workers amid manpower agency dispute
items.desc: Malaysia suspended biomedical health screenings for new Nepali migrants on October 1, effectively halting calling visas after Nepal rejected Kuala Lumpur’s policy restricting recruitment to 25 primary manpower agencies.

items.title: Nepali worker’s death in Saudi Arabia leaves family deep in debt
items.desc: Bharat Mahato’s earnings had sustained his household and financed a new home. Now his wife is left to raise four children and repay Rs1.1 million loan.

items.title: Nuwakot flood victims form struggle committee to pressure federal government for help
items.desc: Victims decry the lackadaisical approach from Kathmandu to the resettlement of displaced people, only prolonging their plight.

items.title: Karnali Yaks stun Janakpur Bolts with late bowling collapse
items.desc: Unish Bikram Singh Thakuri and Hussain Talat take three wickets each as Karnali defend 132 to begin their Nepal Premier League campaign with a 19-run win.

items.title: Colombia announces withdrawal from Hague Group, citing body’s actions over Israel
items.desc: The Hague ​Group of countries ​says it seeks to uphold international law and processes, including ​in the International Criminal ​Court over Israel’s actions.

items.title: Roads around Kirtipur cricket ground to be blacktopped within three months
items.desc: The Kathmandu Road Division has invited bids for upgrading 1.5km of access roads at an estimated cost of Rs69.8 million, ahead of international cricket tournaments.

items.title: Janakpur bowlers restrict Karnali to 132
items.desc: Captain Harmeet Singh takes three wickets as Karnali Yaks lose nine wickets in their 20 overs in the Nepal Premier League.

items.title: Kathmandu Valley to consume 5.18 million flower garlands this Tihar
items.desc: Domestic growers are expected to meet nearly 89 percent of demand as the festival’s flower trade, including plants and potted chrysanthemums, approaches Rs645 million.

items.title: Nepali lawmaker faces privacy backlash over videos of children filmed with smart glasses
items.desc: Ashika Tamang blurred a child’s face after criticism, but rights advocates say her videos raise wider questions about consent and the responsibilities of elected representatives.

items.title: Budhigandaki needs commitment, not another new plan
items.desc: Repeated shifts in financing and implementation have delayed Nepal’s largest reservoir project.

items.title: Who does Nepal Police serve?
items.desc: Is police power guided by law, evidence and accountable command, or by obedience to whoever happens to hold power?

items.title: Attackers kill 60 people in Ethiopia’s conflict-hit Oromiya region, Orthodox church says
items.desc: The ​Holy Synod of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church said ​14 believers were killed in Merti Woreda on October 20 and 46 in Sherka Woreda on October 24.

items.title: Drones came after Lirung. Nepal needs them before the next collapse
items.desc: In Nepal, researchers still need permission for each project to use drones that monitor dangerous slopes before they fail.

items.title: Fastest turnout in 45 years as Israelis pass wartime judgment on Netanyahu
items.desc: The Central Elections Committee reported that 16.7 percent of eligible voters had already cast their ballots within the first three hours, the fastest early turnout rate since 1981.
